description: How the parts library finds each paper doll category's options, maps, palettes and colour areas, by its path below the sex's paper doll root. Ours: the client's paper doll is Python. Derived: the content does not state these rules. Each was found from the content (build 3670638) and from the sources that read it before the parts library did (character-structure-and-plugins.md R5). options: type, one option per .type, named by its file; folder, one option per first-level folder, whose .types name the bloodlines that wear it (underwear: telling it from the content would mean reading every .type); self, the category folder is its one option (skin tone). maps: name, a variation's map replaces the part folder's of the same name (map decals); composed, the composed names in the option's folder; catalog, one map per stem directly in the part folder, with no variation; garment, the garment name lists, the variation folder first; variation, the composed names of the variation folder, else the part folder (hair; moved from Graphene, derived); accessory, by region and role across the item's folders: its variation's, its part's, its metadata's alternativeTextureSourcePath and the one holding its types/ (accessories; derived, with an unqualified-name fallback behind the characterAccessoryMapFallback setting). palettes: own, the .color files directly in the option's folder; shared, those and the category's colors/ (female eye shadow ships a colors/ too, which is not offered: its options keep their own); variant, its own where its .type's colour variant names one, else the category's colors/ (hair; derived); folders, the .color files of an accessory's folders (derived); styles, every option's colour-variant (else default) palette, the option's own first (beards; any style may wear any style's, moved from Graphene, derived). areas: how its colour areas are found (FetchColorAreas): zone, detail, count (the metadata's numColorAreas where stated, else as detail; derived), stated (the part metadata's numColorAreas where stated and a palette ships, else none; accessories, derived) or none. Every category that ships .type files is listed. An empty rule is no rule: the content has not been surveyed for it (the mesh parts, and categories no paper doll part reads), and the query for it throws. head has no option rule: a head is a folder whose options the archetype decides. An archetype is one option per folder. accessories/piercings repeats type names across its folders (stud02 in five) and its types name parts the index does not hold (accessories/earslow/stud02; build 3670638), so its option ids are not unique. requiresModel: an option is offered only when its part ships a mesh; skipPatternedPalettes: a patterned palette is not offered, since nothing composes its pattern yet (accessories; both moved from Graphene, derived). defaultColors: the colours of areas 1 to 3 for an option that takes no palette; the lashes ship none, and are black (moved from Graphene's demo palette, derived). parts: each paper doll part (a CjsPaperDollDefinition member) and the category path it reads; a recipe entry in a category below that path with a maps rule and no part of its own is the part's too (tattoo: tattoo/head; skin: skintone/basic). Edit freely: the engine reads this file as data; a library's generic categories override it by name.
